learning: Iteration 8 showed that the kp 2.2 with kd 0.3 controller reduced line-loss events from 1.0 to 0.05 on the S-bend and slalom, while the oval stayed at 0. Iteration 9 tests whether continuing the damping trend (kd 0.35) removes the rest. If events stay at 0.05 or max_error stays near 0.061 m, damping is no longer the limit and the next geometry lever is wheel_track 0.12 m.
notes: Iteration 8 geometry held exactly; controller moves only kd from 0.30 to 0.35 to test whether more damping clears the residual 0.05 S-bend and slalom line-loss events and brings max_error below 0.06 m.
rationale:
Iteration 8 is the best raced design (88.24). Its geometry (seven 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m) has been held since iteration 5, and the controller change from iteration 7 to 8 (kp 2.8 to 2.2, kd 0.25 to 0.30, ki 0) cut S-bend and slalom line-loss events from 1.0 to 0.05 each. The oval still logs 0 losses, so the span is settled. The remaining problem is max_error at 0.061 to 0.062 m, which sits just above the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit. Body width cannot move that limit, and mass has had no measurable effect.

The trend suggests that more damping at bend onset helps. I keep the iteration 8 geometry exactly, since the Builder holds it as the controlled variable. For the controller I keep kp 2.2, ki 0 and base_speed 1.1, and raise kd from 0.30 to 0.35 to test whether further damping removes the last 0.05 line-loss events per bend track and pulls max_error below 0.06 m. I keep last_direction line-loss handling so that the change is limited to kd. Expected result: S-bend and slalom line-loss events fall to 0, and max_error falls toward 0.06 m. If kd 0.35 adds oscillation instead, the controller falls back to kd 0.30 in the next iteration.
